The Euler-row determinant is exactly \(-(3d-2)^2(2d-2)FD\), a nonzero constant times the reduced defining equation; Saito's criterion proves freeness with degrees \(d\) and \(2d-3\). The cubic assertion follows from a separable degree-two central projection and four simple branch points by Riemann–Hurwitz. Exact symbolic checks were executed for \(d=3,4,5\); they corroborate the universally quantified algebra, which is proven without finite extrapolation. The result explicitly excludes nonreduced inputs and characteristic-positive degeneracies.

originality.rationale: The precise all-degree claim is freeness of the discriminant completion \(F(Q^2-4LR)\) with explicit exponents and homogeneous syzygy basis, not freeness of arbitrary line additions. Dimca et al. treat specific tangent additions, and their projection theorem explicitly places the center outside the base curve. Di Gennaro et al. establish powerful general finite-eigenscheme and pencil-factor criteria, but the first derivation here has the entire curve \(F\) in its eigenscheme (all Euler minors share \(F\)), and the present product is not asserted to be a union of their same-degree pencil members. Vallès assumes a smooth base locus of a same-degree pencil. Bannai–Tokunaga concern topological arrangements; only abstract/excerpt material was available for the most specific comparison, leaving a genuine residual risk. No inspected source or matching mathematical database record established the universal formula; absence of a retrieved match is not a uniqueness proof.

value.rationale: This gives a constructive, all-degree closure operation for a natural geometric class: the residual double cover of a line pencil through a multiplicity-\(d-2\) point. It turns its intrinsically defined branch-direction divisor into an explicit free divisor, without a genericity or quasihomogeneity hypothesis. The special case of every smooth plane cubic and every projection center yields a four-line geometric freeness theorem, including nonflex centers not addressed by the outside-center construction. This is stronger than a symbolic identity or an arbitrary slice: it supplies a free-curve family of unbounded degree, explicit exponent control and a two-generator basis. Residual value risk is overlap with a broader unstated or unindexed freeness construction.
